title: Methods of density functional theory in one dimension
abstract: Density functional theory is formally justified by an existence proof. As such, the need for computational methods to study the theory is a useful route to understanding the full theory. In this paper, we discuss the numerical strategies to efficiently evaluate computations for Kohn-Sham systems in one dimension and also methods for determining exact properties, including time-dependence. An accompanying library is also available for computing one-dimensional density functional theory and publicly available. The expressions used to implement the density functional in one-dimension are surveyed. An alternative justification for a gradient-based technique is also shown that can be applied to time-dependent evolution of the exact Kohn-Sham potential.
summary: This paper details the numerical and theoretical methods for applying Density Functional Theory to one-dimensional quantum systems. By simplifying the dimensionality, the authors develop efficient computational strategies for calculating key energy components, particularly focusing on the exchange and correlation energies within the LDA framework. This work is crucial for advancing the understanding of strongly correlated electron behavior in low dimensions.
main_problem: The paper discusses developing efficient numerical strategies to evaluate Density Functional Theory (DFT) computations for Kohn-Sham systems, specifically focusing on the one-dimensional case to gain insight into the general theory.
main_result: The 1D reduction allows for the study of exact functional relationships in DFT, and the use of an exponential interaction proves highly efficient for advanced numerical methods like DMRG.
method: The authors employ the Kohn-Sham formalism, utilizing techniques like Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT) for calculating Hartree energy and applying the Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) for solving the interacting system.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum systems modeled by DFT, simplified to one dimension. The Hamiltonian includes kinetic, external, and electron-electron interaction terms, with various soft-Coulomb or exponential interactions considered.
key_observables: One-body density $\rho(r)$, total energy components ($T[n], U[n], E_x[n], E_c[n]$), and the Kohn-Sham potential $\text{vs}[n](x)$.
important_parameters: The dimensionality (1D), the interaction potential form (e.g., exponential decay $\exp(-\lambda|x-x'|)$), and density regimes (low- and high-density limits).
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions involve restricting the problem to 1D and employing the Local Density Approximation (LDA) when calculating exchange and correlation energies.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from the general DFT framework to the 1D simplification, details the computational implementation of energy components (Hartree, Exchange, Correlation), and concludes by analyzing the asymptotic limits of the exchange energy.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of DFT methods, especially the focus on 1D systems and the use of advanced numerical techniques like DMRG, provides a valuable theoretical benchmark for understanding correlation effects in low-dimensional quantum matter.
